definition: A Rust Calculation is a pure native function over explicitly supplied UInt64 values. It neither reads storage nor calls another metatype implicitly.
signature: Every declared input is a borrowed u64 parameter and the result is Result<u64, CalculationError>. V1 safe-integer literals and V2 canonical decimal string literals are lowered to exact u64 literals.
arithmetic: Addition, subtraction and multiplication use checked operations. Division rejects zero; reject mode also rejects a nonzero remainder, while floor and ceil are explicit and ceil uses checked increment. No panic, wrapping, saturation, float conversion or narrowing is permitted.
ownership: Inputs are immutably borrowed and outputs are Copy scalar values. The generated function cannot mutate or retain its inputs.
module: One collision-free module per qualified selector under src/domain/calculations. Source identity, contract digest and protocol identity are constants in that module.
verification: Deterministic planning, native Cargo compilation, exact full-width execution, every failure class and stale or malformed selection controls are required.
compatibility: The source schemas and existing generators remain unchanged. This candidate is selected only by the reconciled Rust path and has no default cutover.
